summary.final_text:
The Bradford assay ran and the plate was read at 595 nm.

**What I did:**
1. Took 10 µL of the unknown protein sample (reagents:A4) with a fresh tip and dispensed it into assay_plate:A1.
2. Took 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent (reagents:A3) with a second fresh tip and dispensed it into the same well, A1.
3. Read the whole plate at 595 nm.

**Result:** Well A1 read an absorbance of **0.3138**. The rest of the plate, which has no sample or standard, reads about 0.04–0.06, as expected for blanks.

This is a single raw reading. I did not run a BSA standard curve, so I can't convert A1 to a protein concentration from this run alone.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
